idiom_name: safe navigation &. with Hash#dig and Enumerable#filter_map / #flat_map
implementation_notes: Ruby's safe navigation operator &. skips a method call whose receiver is nil and returns nil, and Hash#dig/Array#dig walk nested structures returning nil when any intermediate step is missing; together they are the 0..1 focus. The plural traversal is Enumerable#filter_map, which keeps the truthy block results (so returning nil means no target), and #flat_map, which maps and flattens one level; the classic optic structure is replaced by these methods. They return new arrays, so use each/each_index when the update must be in place.
code_sketch:
city = order&.customer&.address&.city || "unknown"      # 0..1

# 0..n: keep truthy results, flatten one level
repriced = order.lines.filter_map do |line|
  { name: line[:name], price: discount(line[:price]) } if line
end
pitfalls: &. skips exactly one call, so every level that may be nil needs its own operator; a single missing one raises NoMethodError.
dig cannot distinguish a missing key from a key whose value is nil, so absent and present-but-nil collapse into the same result.
filter_map keeps truthy results only, so a block that legitimately returns false, 0 or an empty string drops those elements.
